Distinguish normal and large text thresholds

WCAG AA has different thresholds for different text sizes; rounded display values do not decide a pass.

Vijeron · Updated 10 October 2026

Normal text

For normal text, WCAG AA minimum contrast is 4.5:1. Measure the actual foreground and background, including link or button states. A ratio of 4.49:1 does not meet 4.5 even if a display rounds it to 4.5.

Large text

Text meeting WCAG's large-scale definition has a 3:1 AA threshold. Large-scale depends on size and weight, not a CSS class name alone. If the rendered size is uncertain, using the normal-text threshold is a safer design choice.

Passing is not the whole experience

A ratio above the minimum may still feel difficult with thin fonts, antialiasing or particular screens. Inspect the actual size and relevant hover, focus and disabled states.

Reproducible example

A 4.7:1 pair meets AA for normal text. A 3.4:1 pair may meet AA for large text but not normal text.

What to check

Do not call 4.49:1 a pass after rounding the displayed number to one decimal.
